Question Choices: Each small square on the grid equals 1 square unit. If a rectangle covers 10 small squares, what is its area?
Hints: Count equal-size squares covering the surface without gaps or overlaps.
Solution: Ten one-square-unit tiles cover 10 square units.

Question Choices: Which rectangle has the same area as rectangle with 1 unit by 8 units?  (A) Rectangle with 2 units by 4 units  (B) Rectangle with 3 units by 4 units   (C) Rectangle with 5 units by 2 units
Hints: Compare products of the side lengths; different pairs can have the same product.
Solution: The given area is 1 x 8 = 8 square units. A: 2 x 4 = 8; B: 3 x 4 = 12; C: 5 x 2 = 10. Only A matches.

Question Choices: Select. There are 2 rectangles. Both have 10 square units of area. Do they have to have the same length and width? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Try multiplying 1 by 10 and 2 by 5. Compare their areas and their side lengths.
Solution: No. A rectangle 1 unit by 10 units has area 1 x 10 = 10 square units. A rectangle 2 units by 5 units has area 2 x 5 = 10 square units. Their side lengths differ even though their areas match.

Question Choices: A rectangle is 3 units long and has area 6 square units. How wide is it?
Hints: Divide area by the known side length. The result is a length.
Solution: Divide area by the known side: 6 divided by 3 = 2 units. Check: 3 x 2 = 6. A side length uses linear units.
